# Jubilees Chapter 26 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** Jacob steals Esau's blessing

---

**26:1** In the forty-third jubilee, in the sixth year of the seventh week, Isaac called his son Esau and said to him: "I am old, and my eyes are dim, and I do not know the day of my death.

**26:2** Now take your weapons — your quiver and your bow — and go out to the field and hunt game for me. Make me savory food that I love, and bring it to me that I may eat, so that my soul may bless you before I die."

**26:3** Rebekah heard when Isaac spoke to his son Esau. And Esau went out early to the field to hunt game and bring it to his father.

**26:4** Rebekah called her son Jacob and said to him: "Behold, I heard your father say to your brother Esau: 'Hunt game for me and make me savory food, and bring it to me that I may eat and bless you before the LORD before my death.'

**26:5** Now therefore, my son, listen to me and do what I command you. Go to the flock and bring me two good young goats, and I will make them into savory food for your father, such as he loves.

**26:6** You shall bring it to your father so that he may eat and bless you before his death."

**26:7** Jacob said to his mother Rebekah: "I am afraid, for my brother Esau is a hairy man and I am smooth-skinned.

**26:8** Perhaps my father will feel me and I will seem to him like a deceiver, and I will bring a curse upon myself and not a blessing."

**26:9** His mother said to him: "Your curse be upon me, my son; only obey my voice."

**26:10** Jacob obeyed his mother Rebekah's voice and went and took two good young goats and brought them to his mother. And his mother made of them savory food such as his father loved.

**26:11** Then Rebekah took the finest garments of her older son Esau, which were with her in the house, and clothed her younger son Jacob with them.

**26:12** She put the skins of the young goats on his hands and on the smooth of his neck.

**26:13** She gave the savory food and the bread she had prepared into the hand of her son Jacob.

**26:14** Jacob came to his father and said: "My father." He said: "Here I am. Who are you, my son?"

**26:15** Jacob said to his father: "I am Esau your firstborn. I have done as you told me. Arise, please; sit and eat of my game, so that your soul may bless me."

**26:16** Isaac said to his son: "How did you find it so quickly, my son?" He said: "Because the LORD your God caused it to come before me."

**26:17** Isaac said to Jacob: "Come near so that I may feel you, my son, whether you are truly my son Esau or not."

**26:18** Jacob came near to his father Isaac, and he felt him and said: "The voice is the voice of Jacob, but the hands are the hands of Esau." He did not recognize him, because his hands were hairy like those of his brother Esau.

**26:19** He blessed him and said: "Are you truly my son Esau?" He said: "I am."

**26:20** He said: "Bring it near to me that I may eat of my son's game, so that my soul may bless you." He brought it to him and he ate; and he brought him wine and he drank.

**26:21** His father Isaac said to him: "Come near and kiss me, my son." He came near and kissed him, and he smelled the scent of his garments and blessed him.

**26:22** He said: "See, the scent of my son is like the scent of a fruitful field that the LORD has blessed. May God give you of the dew of heaven and of the richness of the earth, and abundance of grain and new wine.

**26:23** May peoples serve you, and nations bow down to you. Be lord over your brothers, and let your mother's sons bow down to you. Cursed be everyone who curses you, and blessed be everyone who blesses you."

**26:24** As soon as Isaac had finished blessing his son Jacob, and Jacob had just gone out from before his father Isaac, his brother Esau came in from his hunting.

**26:25** He also made savory food and brought it to his father, saying: "Let my father arise and eat of his son's game, so that your soul may bless me."

**26:26** His father Isaac said to him: "Who are you?" He answered: "I am your son, your firstborn, Esau."

**26:27** Then Isaac trembled with a very great trembling and said: "Who then was it who hunted game and brought it to me? I ate of all of it before you came, and I blessed him — and indeed he shall be blessed."

**26:28** When Esau heard the words of his father Isaac, he cried out with an exceedingly great and bitter cry and said to his father: "Bless me also, my father."

**26:29** He said: "Your brother came with deceit and has taken your blessing."

**26:30** Esau said: "Is he not rightly named Jacob? For he has supplanted me these two times: he took my birthright, and now he has taken my blessing." He said: "Have you not reserved a blessing for me?"

**26:31** Isaac answered and said to Esau: "Behold, I have made him your lord, and all his brothers I have given him as servants, and I have sustained him with grain and new wine. What then can I do for you, my son?"

**26:32** Esau said to his father: "Have you only one blessing, my father? Bless me, even me also, my father." Esau lifted up his voice and wept.

**26:33** Then his father Isaac answered him: "Behold, far from the richness of the earth shall your dwelling be, and far from the dew of heaven above.

**26:34** By your sword you shall live, and you shall serve your brother. But when you grow restless, you shall break his yoke from your neck."

---

*SOPHIA notes: Consensus rendering. The formal LOGOS base text was adopted throughout with EMET adjustments for "savory food," "new wine," and the blessing formula. PNEUMA's dramatic rendering of the dialogue was consulted but the formal register was preferred to maintain the solemnity of the blessing scene. Key divergences logged in disagreement file.*
